summary: Russian forces launched a massive overnight barrage of Geran-5 missiles and Shahed drones from multiple axes targeting at least 14 Ukrainian regions, with Ukrainian air defenses engaging over Kyiv. The attacks caused 22 casualties in Zaporizhzhia including three children, and killed two civilians in Chernihiv region's Mena. Simultaneously, Ukrainian strikes hit the Samara oil facility processing 50% of Russia's export blend and the Lipetsk-2 airfield command post, while ballistic missile threats against energy infrastructure were extended 48 hours.
key_points: Russian forces launched mass Geran-5 missile and Shahed drone attack across 14+ Ukrainian regions overnight Nov 14-15, 2026. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/78214)
Ukrainian air defenses intercepted targets over Kyiv; air raid alert lasted from 01:18 to 03:30 Nov 15. (Source: @eRadarrua/130702)
Zaporizhzhia attack wounded 22 including three children aged 6 months, 2 and 12 years. (Source: @UkraineNow/85305)
Russian drone strike killed two men (42, 45) and injured one (33) in Mena, Chernihiv region. (Source: @eRadarrua/130668)
Ukrainian strikes hit Samara oil facility (50% of Russia's export blend) and Lipetsk-2 airfield command post. (Source: @eRadarrua/130647)
Ballistic missile threat extended 48 hours targeting energy infrastructure in Kyiv, Poltava, Kharkiv, Dnipropetrovsk regions. (Source: @eRadarrua/130686)
US plans to cut European troop presence from 25,000 to 5,000; Bulgaria suspends military aid to Ukraine. (Source: @UkraineNow/85310)
Putin demands UK renounce nuclear deterrent; Ukraine-Canada agree to strengthen air defense and long-range capabilities. (Source: @UkraineNow/85308)

sections.executive_summary: Russian forces executed a large-scale coordinated strike using Geran-5 missiles and Shahed drones launched from Orel, Kursk, Bryansk, the Black Sea, and occupied territories against at least 14 Ukrainian oblasts overnight November 14-15. Ukrainian air defenses intercepted multiple targets over Kyiv during a two-hour air raid alert, while strikes caused 22 injuries in Zaporizhzhia including three children and two deaths in Chernihiv's Mena. Concurrently, Ukrainian deep strikes damaged the Samara oil hub handling half of Russia's crude exports and the Lipetsk-2 airfield command post, as ballistic missile threats to energy infrastructure were extended.

points: Ukrainian air defenses intercepted multiple aerial targets over Kyiv during an air raid alert lasting from 01:18 to 03:30 on November 15, with at least one Geran-5 missile entering the Darnytskyi district before being engaged. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/78233, @eRadarrua/130702, @eRadarrua/130724)

The Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) and General Staff conducted a precision strike on the Samara linear production dispatching station near Prosviet, hitting oil reservoirs and causing a large fire; the facility processes Urals blend accounting for approximately 50% of Russia's oil exports. (Source: @eRadarrua/130647)

Ukrainian forces also struck the Lipetsk-2 airfield in Lipetsk region, damaging a hangar with specialized aircraft maintenance equipment, a fuel reservoir, and the central command post. (Source: @UkraineNow/85301)

A Russian drone attack on Zaporizhzhia wounded 22 civilians, including three children: a 6-month-old infant, a 2-year-old girl, and a 12-year-old boy, during a repeat strike on the city. (Source: @UkraineNow/85305)
In Hlukhiv, a police officer shielded a 9-year-old boy with his body during a repeated drone attack, preventing injury to the child. (Source: @UkraineNow/85304)

Ukraine and Canada held discussions on strengthening air defense systems and long-range strike capabilities, with Ukrainian officials thanking Canada for continued support. (Source: @UkraineNow/85307)

US senators demanded Elon Musk preserve documents regarding Starlink restrictions for Ukraine, seeking correspondence between SpaceX, the White House, and the Pentagon by November 30. (Source: @UkraineNow/85295)

Russian forces launched a massive coordinated barrage overnight November 14-15, employing Geran-5 cruise missiles and Shahed-type one-way attack drones from at least five launch areas: Orel (2 reactive groups), Kursk (8 groups), Bryansk, the Black Sea, and occupied territories in Donetsk, Kherson, and Zaporizhzhia regions. (Source: @eRadarrua/130676, @mon1tor_ua/78214, @kpszsu/96128)

Targets spanned at least 14 Ukrainian oblasts: Kyiv, Chernihiv, Sumy, Poltava, Kharkiv, Dnipropetrovsk, Kirovohrad, Cherkasy, Vinnytsia, Zhytomyr, Khmelnytskyi, Chernivtsi, Mykolaiv, and Odesa, with missiles observed circling over Kyiv, Poltava, Kropyvnytskyi, Shepetivka, and Slavuta. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/78214, @mon1tor_ua/78222, @mon1tor_ua/78223, @mon1tor_ua/78226, @mon1tor_ua/78239, @mon1tor_ua/78240)

Specific launches included three reactive Shaheds from Dnipropetrovsk toward Poltava's Kremenchuk district, one reactive Shahed from Mykolaiv toward Kropyvnytskyi, one Geran-5 from Bryansk to Chernihiv district, and one Geran-5 from Sumy to Novhorod-Siverskyi district. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/78214)

A Russian drone strike on critical infrastructure in Mena, Chernihiv region, killed two men aged 42 and 45 and injured a 33-year-old man, with casualty figures still being clarified. (Source: @eRadarrua/130668)

Russian authorities extended the elevated ballistic missile threat for 48 hours, explicitly targeting energy infrastructure in Kyiv, Poltava, Kharkiv, and Dnipropetrovsk regions, urging civilians to prepare alternative power and water supplies. (Source: @eRadarrua/130686)

Vladimir Putin issued an ultimatum to the United Kingdom demanding renunciation of its nuclear deterrent, linking the demand to proposed negotiations on ending the war in Ukraine. (Source: @UkraineNow/85308)

Russian air defense and electronic warfare assets attempted to counter Ukrainian strikes on the Samara oil facility and Lipetsk-2 airfield, though the extent of interception is unconfirmed. (Source: @eRadarrua/130647, @UkraineNow/85301)

Russian forces launched a reactive UAV from occupied Donetsk region toward Kharkiv oblast, specifically targeting the Lozova area, indicating continued use of forward positions for deep strikes. (Source: @kpszsu/96128)

Dnipropetrovsk region hosted at least two groups of reactive UAVs that were tracked moving toward Poltava oblast's Kremenchuk district, suggesting the region serves as a launch or transit corridor. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/78214, @eRadarrua/130665)

Russian air defense radar emissions and UAV launch activity were detected in the vicinity of the Donetsk-Zaporizhzhia contact line, though no ground maneuver details were reported in the source messages. (Source: @eRadarrua/130673, @kpszsu/96128)

Ukrainian monitoring channels reported multiple reactive UAV groups in Dnipropetrovsk and Kharkiv oblasts, consistent with Russian preparation for sustained long-range strike campaigns against rear-area logistics and energy nodes. (Source: @eRadarrua/130665, @eRadarrua/130673)

No specific ground combat engagements, territorial changes, or artillery duels were detailed in the provided messages for the eastern front during this reporting period. (Source: @mon1tor_ua, @kpszsu, @eRadarrua)

The intensity of UAV launches from eastern occupied territories suggests Russian forces maintain robust aerial strike capacity despite Ukrainian counter-battery and air defense efforts. (Source: @eRadarrua/130676, @mon1tor_ua/78214)
Ukrainian strike on Lipetsk-2 airfield, while not on the eastern front, demonstrates Kyiv's ability to target Russian aviation assets supporting eastern operations. (Source: @UkraineNow/85301)

Russian forces launched Geran-5 missiles from Bryansk region toward Chernihiv oblast's Chernihiv district and from Sumy region toward Novhorod-Siverskyi district, demonstrating cross-border strike capability from Russian territory. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/78214)

A Geran-5 missile was launched from Kursk region toward Sumy oblast's Sumy district, while reactive UAV groups were reported launched from Orel (2 groups) and Kursk (8 groups) toward northern Ukrainian regions. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/78225, @eRadarrua/130676)

Ukrainian air defense tracked a reactive UAV from Chernihiv region toward Kyiv oblast's Vyshhorod district, and another from Chernihiv toward Kyiv's Ivankiv area, indicating Russian use of occupied or border areas for penetration routes. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/78237, @kpszsu/96146)

Chernihiv and Sumy oblasts hosted multiple reactive UAV groups and "Molniya"-type UAVs, with eRadarrua reporting two strike UAV groups and one reactive group in Sumy, and one reactive group in Chernihiv. (Source: @eRadarrua/130683, @eRadarrua/130691)

Kyiv city and oblast endured an air raid alert from 01:18 to 03:30 on November 15, with multiple Geran-5 missiles and reactive Shaheds approaching from the northeast and east, including overflying Brovary and circling near Boryspil and Vasylkiv. (Source: @eRadarrua/130702, @mon1tor_ua/78213, @mon1tor_ua/78231, @mon1tor_ua/78232)

Ballistic missile threat was specifically extended for 48 hours against energy infrastructure in Kyiv, Poltava, Kharkiv, and Dnipropetrovsk oblasts, heightening alert posture across the northern and northeastern approaches. (Source: @eRadarrua/130686)
No ground incursions or artillery strikes on border settlements were reported in the messages for this period. (Source: @mon1tor_ua, @kpszsu, @eRadarrua)

Multiple UAV groups launched from the Black Sea targeted Odesa oblast, with courses toward Chornomorsk, Karolino-Buhaz, Hrybivka, and Lymanka, indicating sustained maritime launch capability. (Source: @kpszsu/96107, @kpszsu/96115, @kpszsu/96135)

A reactive Shahed launched from Mykolaiv oblast targeted Kirovohrad oblast's Kropyvnytskyi district from the south-southeast, while another group of reactive UAVs moved from Mykolaiv toward Kropyvnytskyi from the north. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/78214, @kpszsu/96111, @kpszsu/96118, @kpszsu/96120)
Odesa oblast served as a launch point for a group of reactive UAVs heading toward Vinnytsia oblast, demonstrating Russian use of occupied coastal territory for deep strikes. (Source: @kpszsu/96141
